bug_semantics: Before application WebSock callbacks run, Bandit's RFC 6455 fragmented-message path retains the initial non-final Text/Binary payload and appends every non-final Continuation payload to per-connection fragment_frame.data without a cumulative message-size limit. An unauthenticated peer can therefore keep fin false indefinitely and make retained BEAM memory grow with attacker-controlled bytes; finishing the message additionally flattens the accumulated iodata. The per-frame max_frame_size does not bound the sum across frames.
flaw_origin: Commit 8909391f486d42138c5308410bc5ea49a65f4d46 first implemented WebSocket continuation-frame reassembly in lib/bandit/websocket/connection.ex. It added fragment_frame state, stored non-final Text/Binary frames, and concatenated each Continuation payload into that state with no cumulative byte check. Commit 6ab40a1ca44e7877b1c57d387727574d9c1e4957 later changed binary concatenation to iodata for performance, but preserved the already-unbounded mechanism and is therefore a refactor, not the BIC.
ai_marker: absent: the exact raw BIC commit object names author Mat Trudel <mat@geeky.net> and committer Mat Trudel <mat@geeky.net>, has the sole message 'Implement continuation frames', and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI-attribution trailer/marker.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/mtrudel/bandit/security/advisories/GHSA-pf94-94m9-536p identifies lib/bandit/websocket/connection.ex handle_frame/3, the unbounded continuation accumulator, affected range >=0.5.0 and <1.11.0, patched version 1.11.0, and links fix https://github.com/mtrudel/bandit/commit/21612c7c7b1ce43eccd36d3af3a2299d23513667. In the validated clone, git log -L 90,114:lib/bandit/websocket/connection.ex at the fix parent traces the fragment handler through 6ab40a1ca44e7877b1c57d387727574d9c1e4957 to 8909391f486d42138c5308410bc5ea49a65f4d46; git -S searches for fragment_frame and both accumulator forms corroborate that WebSocket origin. The BIC diff adds fragment_frame and the non-final Continuation branch in lib/bandit/websocket/connection.ex, including unbounded connection.fragment_frame.data <> frame.data. Direct-parent tree verification against 18c7030616bfecff3cd78a72362c600a3365ca63 found no fragment_frame, Frame.Continuation, or iodata_to_binary occurrence in that path, while the parent-to-BIC diff shows the complete reassembly state and branches being added. Version checks found tag 0.5.0 at 102adfd56bd4aacd39469a5582104377618abc9f does not contain the BIC and its connection.ex has no fragment reassembly; tag 0.5.1 at 8029d15762c3658b504913d39aa91ba23091171c does contain it and is the first affected tagged release observed, so the advisory's inclusive 0.5.0 lower bound is broader than repository history supports. Tag 1.10.4 at dea432ec1ec94eee4b9ad0219b09a568c4ccb960 contains the unbounded accumulator and does not contain the fix. Fix 21612c7c7b1ce43eccd36d3af3a2299d23513667 directly adds max_fragmented_message_size with an 8,000,000-byte default, checks both final and non-final continuation accumulation, and closes oversize messages with RFC 6455 code 1009. Tag 1.11.0 at e62619895d0d2584d7ffa57d43ef6f72437dfaff contains that fix; first-party release https://github.com/mtrudel/bandit/releases/tag/1.11.0 resolves to that tag commit. Finally, numactl-prefixed git cat-file commit on the BIC produced a single-parent commit object with human author/committer Mat Trudel and no trailers or AI markers.
reasoning: The causal flaw is unbounded aggregate message retention, not the later choice of binary versus iodata representation. The smallest commit that created the exploitable WebSocket lifecycle is 8909391f486d42138c5308410bc5ea49a65f4d46: it first accepted a non-final data frame into connection state and repeatedly enlarged that state for continuations without enforcing an aggregate limit. Its immediate parent cannot take this path because the state field and all WebSocket continuation handling are absent. The 2023 performance commit only rewrites the same accumulation and does not originate the vulnerability. Release ancestry places the mechanism in 0.5.1 through 1.10.4, while 0.5.0 lacks it; the first-party advisory is correct at the fixed upper boundary but overstates the lower boundary. Commit 21612c7c7b1ce43eccd36d3af3a2299d23513667 is both the advisory-linked and direct source fix and is included in 1.11.0. Because the exact BIC commit object has only a human author/committer and no AI attribution marker, the BIC-only attribution rule yields NOT_AI.
